abstract.p: Computerized Adaptive Testing is a widely used technology for evaluating examinees' proficiency in online education platforms. By leveraging prior estimates of proficiency to select questions and updating the estimates iteratively based on responses, it enables personalized examinee modeling and has attracted substantial attention. Despite this progress, most existing works focus primarily on improving proficiency estimation accuracy, while overlooking the selection bias inherent in the adaptive process. Selection bias arises because the question selection is strongly influenced by the estimated proficiency, such as assigning easier questions to examinees with lower proficiency and harder ones to examinees with higher proficiency. Since the selection depends on prior estimation, this bias propagates into the diagnostic model, which is further amplified during iterative updates, leading to misaligned and biased predictions. Moreover, the imbalance in examinees' historical interactions often exacerbates bias in diagnostic models.
